newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends off on light profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends off on light profit-taking.

text.p: NYMEX crude ended lower Thursday after traders booked some profits from Tuesday's rally following the New Year holiday.
"It's basically profit-taking as there was no real news anywhere," said Nauman Barakat, trader with Prudential Securities in New York.
Feb crude ended 23 cents off at $25.69 a barrel, but first made a contract high of $26.05 before profit-taking set in.
Heating oil was supported by strength in gas oil futures on London's IPE, but crude capped heat's gains. Feb heating oil settled up 0.04 cent at 72.11 cents a gallon.
January gas oil closed up a sharp $8.25 to $232.00 a tonne on the IPE due to cold weather in Europe.
Gasoline traded slightly higher with some fund buying spotted earlier in the session. February gasoline settled up 0.27 cent at 71.10 cents a gallon.
Volume was light as some traders had not yet returned from the New Year holiday Wednesday.
Traders were also less aggressive as they awaited direction from the American Petroleum Institute's (API) weekly oil inventory data expected out Thursday evening, dealers said.
Analysts and traders said high refiner output was expected to have boosted refined product stocks in the data which reflects the week ended December 27.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk ((212-859-1761))
